utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. There was still a few issues. Ms. Loukas, you asked yesterday special access to the public gallery. I did understand that it's not at this moment urgent any more. I don't know whether you still would like to have a decision on it for days to come.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps for some subsequent occasion, in view of the fact that the witness today is protected, and also I think my niece decided spending the day with her Dutch friends would be more interesting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me say the following: The Chamber was inclined to grant your request, so whenever it becomes relevant again, please address us and then we'll then most likely allow it.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then there was one other issue, communication between the parties in respect of Prosecution Exhibits 200 to 203. Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours, counsel. That's an issue that initially was raised and Mr. Resch was the lawyer who led those exhibits. I'm informed that Mr. Hannis is dealing with that issue. I'm trying to resolve that issue so I can report to Your Honours this afternoon. Mr. Hannis will be in a position to report tomorrow about that particular issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll wait until tomorrow. It's not that urgent, but I just didn't want to lose it out of sight. Then if there are no further procedural issues -- yes, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, in fact there are some procedural issues. Just in relation to this witness, there are a number of matters I wish to place on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Firstly, I received the 89(F) summary by e-mail today, at 1.13, which I would submit is unacceptably late for the current purposes. I would indicate that upon receipt, I indicated to Mr. Margetts the paragraphs, the 89(F) summary, that I objected to, which at this stage I haven't received a response. But in view of the lateness of time, I appreciate that that would not have been easy in the circumstances. I would also indicate that I received a supplemental information sheet at 12.35 today, in relation to this witness. Again, unacceptably late, in my submission. The other aspect is that, in relation to the receipt of material in relation to this particular witness, I can also indicate that I made a number of objections to the statement. The Prosecution have agreed to a number of the paragraphs being redacted, but there's still a number of paragraphs outstanding. And also, further in relation to the question of material on this witness, I would indicate that initially a CD was disclosed last week in relation to this witness, indicating some 86 exhibits, and an e-mail was received last night at 9.00, reducing it to, I think, approximately 26. I do place those matters on the record, Your Honour, because there's been, I would submit, lateness in terms of the selection of the number of exhibits, lateness in terms of the 89(F) summary, and the lateness in terms of the supplemental information sheet. Now, I spoke to Mr. Margetts prior to Your Honours coming on to the Bench, and he indicated that he thought that he'd be about two hours with this witness. In the circumstances, I indicate to Your Honours that it's unlikely that I would be in a position to proceed to cross-examine this witness immediately upon the completion of the evidence in chief. So I place those matters on the record, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Margetts, any response?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Some substantial response, in fact. In respect of the alleged lateness of the 89(F) summary, my learned friend in fact has provided some general complaints in relation to the statement that indicated that she objected to a very substantial portion of the statement. I had requested that she detail the exact paragraphs, which in fact she did, and late yesterday evening I advised that it was not possible for us to provide an 89(F) summary until the discussions between the parties were complete in respect of what that summary would refer to. As soon as it was clear, in fact, what paragraphs we intended to submit in the form of 89(F), we provided the 89(F) summary to the Defence. In respect of the alleged lateness of the supplemental information that was provided at 12.35 today, the witness completed providing that supplemental information at 11.30 today. Immediately that was put in a form that could be provided to the Defence and was provided to them. In regard to the paragraphs that the Defence says they object to, we have a response in respect of each one of those specific paragraphs. It's our submission that they're entirely appropriate for the 89(F) procedure. And in regard to the 86 exhibits that were provided to the Defence almost a week ago, one, they've had substantial time to review them; two, the witness only was in for proofing yesterday and we managed to go through each of those exhibits with the witness; and immediately upon reducing that to a list of 26, we provided that list, that reduced list, to the Defence at 9.00 p.m. last night, the proofing finishing at 8.00 p.m. The nature of those 86 exhibits are in most instances documents that have been disclosed to the Defence for quite some time, and brief documents, one-page minutes of Crisis Staff meetings or War Presidency minutes. So we did not consider that burdensome. In fact, in preparation for this witness we would have considered that advantageous to the Defence. So we do contest any representation that there's been any lateness from the Prosecution. Thirdly, it has been indicated to the Defence that this would be an 89(F) witness. In our view, that's in the interests of justice that we do expedite these proceedings. The statement was adequate, and in our view, there was no necessity for this witness to go through that evidence and take the Court's time. In light of that, we are surprised that the Defence would not be ready to cross-examine, given that the substantial part of the witness's evidence is going to be produced in written form, and for some time they've had notice of that. That's all we have in response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I might briefly respond to Mr. Margetts' --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: -- assertions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But before doing so, Ms. Loukas, I'd like to make one observation. That's the following: I think that the Prosecution is not criticised for waiting too long after they have -- they had their proofing sessions with the witness, that they waited too long to provide the Defence with the results of that, but perhaps that the proofing sessions take place too late, so that finally if you would finish your proofing sessions a quarter of an hour before the hearing starts, then of course you might do it in one or two minutes. But nevertheless, it's 15 minutes before we start. So I think that's the problem. And of course we should ask ourselves, as a matter of efficiency, whether, if we spend 20 minutes on these kind of debates on what's late and what's not late, that is 25 of us or 20 minutes, that's 500 minutes of Registry, interpreters, judges, parties. So if we would have to strike a balance, whether it would be acceptable that the witness would arrive one day earlier and to do everything at least 24 hours early stage, we should consider that. Of course, it's not up to the Chamber to control the budget of the OTP, and I do understand that there are some budgetary restraints, but at the same time we have some time constraints, and we have on average 25 human beings in court listening to debates on the late delivery of summaries, statements, et cetera. Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: In fact, Your Honour has taken up my point in relation to the late arrival of the witnesses, and that is in fact precisely the point. And I have nothing further to add in relation to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll see what's possible this afternoon, what is not. Mr. Margetts, are you ready to start the examination of Witness 144?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We're ready to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we first have to pull the curtains down, because Witness 144 is protected by face and voice distortion, and we use a pseudonym in respect of him. Would it be a solution if I suggest to the parties that we would not start with the 89(F) summary, but keep that perhaps for a later moment and that the parties have an opportunity -- first of all, we'll then know what subjects have been dealt with in viva voce examination. And of course, the Chamber is not aware of what specific paragraphs are subject of the Defence complaints. So therefore, it's difficult for us too. So let's see if the parties can agree on that, and if not, the Chamber would like to be informed about the character of the objections and the -- we then give a decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Just in relation to that, Your Honour, I can indicate that as I indicated earlier, there are outstanding objections in the 89(F) summary, and I'm happy to deal with them in the manner suggested by Your Honour, and the objections related to the substantive statement we can deal with at some later time as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness 144. I call you Witness 144 because protective measures have been granted in respect of you. That means that we'll not use your name, but call you Witness 144, and that the outside world will not see your face and will not hear your voice. Both will be distorted when your testimony is broadcasted to the outside world. Before giving evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration of which the text will now be handed out to you by Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Witness 144. The curtains may be pulled up again. Mr. Margetts, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to present the first exhibit to the witness. If that could be presented under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit number P324, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's a pseudonym sheet, I expect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This pseudonym sheet, you'll note, is not in the typical form of a pseudonym sheet. It has the background of the witness in terms of the witness's employment history. The reason for placing that additional information on this sheet is so that we don't have to go into private session to receive this information. So we'd like that exhibit marked and given a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, I take it that you have been provided with this bit of special --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps then when you could read it at the same time when the witness reads it.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And tell us whether ... Witness, would you please take your time to read the B/C/S part of this document, and also to verify whether your name is on that document. And wait for a second to confirm, because we'll first give an opportunity to Ms. Loukas to verify.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I can indicate, Your Honour, I have no problem with that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You may proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Witness 144, can you see your name on this sheet that is before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to instruct the parties to always put their microphones off when the witness starts answering your questions, because otherwise the voice of the witness would come through the other microphone to the public. So therefore, once you've put the question, please turn your microphone off.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: In the right-hand column of that document is a listing of your experience and your personal details. Is that listing in the right-hand column in Bosnian correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If the pseudonym sheet could be -- thank you, Your Honour. If the pseudonym sheet could be returned. Your Honour, I'd like to present the next exhibit to the witness, and that is the ICTY witness statement of this witness. That too will be presented under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit number P325, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Witness, you have before you a Bosnian version of the statement provided to the Office of the Prosecutor in July 1997. Is that the statement that you provided to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Since you've arrived in The Hague, have you had the opportunity to review this statement, and are the matters set out in the statement true and correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if that statement could be returned. In the ordinary course, I would ask to proceed with the oral summary of the statement, but in light of the objections, we'll proceed at the end of the witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You now may continue the examination viva voce.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I'd like to present the next three exhibits to the witness. They are three maps. The first two maps, I imagine, will be uncontroversial. The first map depicts where the municipality of Kotor Varos lies in Bosnia. The second map depicts the municipality of Kotor Varos. If the Defence has no objection to those maps, then there's no need for them to be presented to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: There's no objection to the maps, Your Honours. I've seen them.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Map number 1 will be Prosecution number P326. Map number 2, P327. And map 3, P328.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: If the third map, the map of Kotor Varos city and surrounds, could be provided to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Witness 144, do you recognise this map, and is this a map that you pre-marked yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Could you refer to the numbering set out on that map, the numbers that run from south to north, 1 through 5, and describe to the Court the various structures that those numbers depict.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Number 1 depicts the house that I used to live in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, if you're asking for protective measures, is this a question that should be dealt -- could we ask for redaction?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If that map could not be displayed on any external monitor, and if the map could be provided under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because -- I don't know where the map is, where it's visible or not for the outside world. Or if not, then it has not been put on an ELMO. So therefore, the damage is limited, because no one knows what 1 stands for. And then P328, was that under seal or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would like it to be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You'd like it to be under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Perhaps you could continue with the witness as long as the map is not on an ELMO or in whatever other form of electronic display to the outside world. You can continue. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Witness 144, if you could just start again to describe what each of those numbers mark on the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Number 1 marks the house in which I lived. Number 2 marks the Municipal Assembly building. Number 3 marks the municipal court and prison. Number 4 marks the police station building. Number 5 marks the elementary school building in which we were detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you estimate for the Court the distance along the road from your house to the building marked 5, which is the school.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes. The distance is between 1.2 and 1.5 kilometres. Therefore, between 1.2 and 1.5 kilometres. That would be the distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you. How far is it from the city of Kotor Varos to the city of Celinac that lies in the north?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: The distance between Kotor Varos and Celinac is about 15 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: How far is it from the city of Kotor Varos to the city of Banja Luka that lies further north along the same road, through Celinac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: The distance between Kotor Varos and Banja Luka is about 31 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We've finished with that exhibit. If the witness could be shown the next two exhibits. That is a document setting out the ethnic composition of Kotor Varos and an assessment of the security situation in the area of Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: They will be P329 and P330.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Witness, could you please refer to the document that is headed "national structure of the population according to local communes."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Can you look at the last row on that table, where, in the total percentage of Croats, Muslims, and Serbs from the municipality of Kotor Varos is set out. Can you tell me whether or not that represents the demographic of the municipality of Kotor Varos before the conflict in 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: If you could look at the next document, which is headed "assessment of security situation in the area of Kotor Varos." Could you read the second paragraph of that document, which commences: "Since 11 June 1992." And ends: "72 per cent Serbs." And could you tell me whether the percentages set out in that paragraph represent the demographics in Kotor Varos as at around May 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: These data are consistent with the demographic picture in the area at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you read the third paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just prior to moving on with this document, I'd just like to -- the way in which it's been used thus far, I would object to any further use of the document, firstly, in terms of the fact that it is not the witness's own document. It's not a document that he's apparently had any association with. There's been no foundation laid for the use of this document via this witness, and I would be objecting on that basis. I'd also indicate, Your Honour, of course we usually deal with objections in relation to documents at the end, but just for the record, again, the document is not signed, it's not -- there's no stamp, there's nothing to indicate its authenticity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a document that purports to set out the situation in Kotor Varos as at May 1993, and it purports to record events that took place from the middle of 1992, events that are pertinent to the indictment in this case. This witness is not able to vouch for the authenticity of this document, and that's not what we present this document to him for. We present this document to him as someone who was present in Kotor Varos from the middle of 1992 and to the middle -- throughout the period to the middle of 1993, and is someone who will be able to assist the Court in assessing whether the information set out in this document is accurate and correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But will you present any evidence or any further information as to the source of this document? Because if the witness can confirm the correctness of some of the content of this document, of course, that means that the witness has some personal knowledge if the document is an authentic document or at least if we know where it comes from, then it -- you could expect some mutual support of the two sources of information. But the complaint of Ms. Loukas is that we do not know where this document comes from.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is another matter of the order in which the evidence is presented.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll hear from you later on what the origin of this document is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So then we'll first wait and see what information comes to the Chamber in this respect. Please proceed. I noticed, Mr. Margetts, that the copy we received of the map is a bit different from the original. All the legends are missing. Ms. Loukas, there are some legends on the original one which do not appear on the copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. The copy that we've received does not have a legend either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Can you do without? I mean, most of it -- what a tree is on the map, even without a legend -- the scale is on the map, which is most important.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I don't think we have a problem --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: -- with the absence of a legend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Margetts, in general terms, if there's a scale on the map and the whole distance is on the map, the Chamber is perfectly able to read distances. And even when it says Celinac is approximately 14 kilometres, then there's no need to ask the witness again, unless there's any reason to believe that's not correct. Banja Luka, however, is not on the map. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Witness 144, I'd like to read to you the second paragraph of the document that is before you, and I will ask your comment in respect of a number of matters. The second paragraph reads as follows: "Referring to the situation from 11 June 1992 that states: "Croats remained in the villages of Zabrdje, Podbrdje, Sibovi, Bastina, Novo Selo. There is a small number of them in Vrbanjci and Orahova and very few in Kotor Varos. These are predominantly elderly people who do not pose any real threat. Out of a total number of Muslims who remained in the municipality, most of them are in Siprage and the surroundings village of Dunici, Denici, Crepovi, Kovacevici, Zuhrici and Palivuk, where they number about 3.500. They are also in Garici and Curkici. A very small number of them live in Vrbanjci and some in Kotor Varos itself. The elderly and children are also predominant in this category, but there are also a good number of able-bodied men. We assess that around 400 people are up to 35 and another 250 to 300 up to 55 years old." Witness, does that set out an accurate representation of the demographic of Croat and Muslim people who had remained in Kotor Varos up to May 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes. These demographics are consistent with the situation in the municipality of Kotor Varos in this period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Witness, I'd like to refer you to the next paragraph in this document, and I'll read this paragraph into the record as well. It states: "Muslims in Garici, Curkici and Vrbanjci were disarmed in July and August 1992. People in the area of Siprage and other villages were disarmed at the end of January and February of the current year. Thus, 318 legally and around 90 pieces of illegally bought weapons, mostly automatic and semi-automatic rifles and several pistols were temporarily confiscated in the area. According to operative information there could be another 15 to 20 pieces of illegal weapons which should not jeopardise the safety of our forces and citizens." Witness, is that consistent with your understanding of what occurred in Kotor Varos in terms of disarmament of the population?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've finished with that document. If the next document could be presented to the witness, and this is a document dated 27 March. And if this document could be presented under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit number P331, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the next couple of questions, could we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session. Please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, could the witness statement be returned to the witness. That's Exhibit numbered 325. And could that remain with him throughout the duration of the examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might just ascertain from Mr. Margetts if the statement is there for the purposes of the witness reading his statement prior to giving answers or if it's there just in case he wants to refer to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the purpose of the statement being there is that when we are referring to specific topics and there are undisputed paragraphs between the Defence and the Prosecution, so it's clear to the witness what matters I am asking him about and what matters are already referred to in his statement, I intend to refer him to his statement and then ask him in relation to further relevant matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it's rather to have a starting point than to seek refreshment of his memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm grateful for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Witness, could I refer you to paragraph 108 of your statement. At paragraph 108, you detail a meeting between yourself, Zdravko Samardzija, Momcilo Komljenovic, and another gentleman, wherein they ordered that all weapons be handed over. Komljenovic told you that the SDS had taken over Kotor Varos --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is precisely what I wanted to avoid. Mr. Margetts is reading out the paragraph as opposed to referring up to the point of a particular meeting and then allowing the witness to give his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, it depends on what questions will come. If, for example, which I do not expect Mr. Margetts would ask the witness to describe those persons present or what they were wearing, then of course it's a good introduction. If however, other questions -- so let's just wait and see. I think I made it quite clear that the Chamber understands the position of Mr. Margetts to be that he introduces the questions and not brings into the mind of the witness what he'd like to hear from him.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Precisely, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, please proceed. And, well, you heard both the objection and the understanding of the Chamber of the way you're proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Komljenovic stated that the SDS had taken over Kotor Varos and that the town was now considered as part of the Serb Republic. You're also told that a Crisis Staff had been formed in order to deal with civilian matters until a proper legal body had been established. Following this meeting with Mr. Komljenovic, which you referred to as a meeting in around mid-June 1992, did you have any further contacts with Mr. Komljenovic in 1992, or did you hear of other contacts that were made with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: I had no further contacts with Komljenovic, and I never heard of anything else that he was involved in. On that day, he came together with Zdravko Samardzija and a couple of other people I did not know, who wore camouflage uniforms. There was a man with them that was familiar to me, Dusko Skoric, who hailed from Kotor Varos. What they told us was that Kotor Varos was now part of the Republic of Srpska, that a Crisis Staff had been established and that people who lived in my neighbourhood were supposed to hand over their weapons, their legally owned weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. When you were detained --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just in relation to that again, it's clear that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Ms. Loukas, I noticed two things. First of all, that Mr. Margetts asked what happened after this meeting, and that the answer of the witness was, apart from a very brief answer to that question, that he then started to describe the meeting again, which was already read out. It was not Mr. Margetts who asked for that. So if I would give any instruction at this moment, Mr. Margetts, I think your question was fully in line with what you were expected to do, but the witness described again what you had already put to him in reading. So perhaps then you could guide the witness just to limit himself to answer the question and not to repeat what you had stated already.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And indeed an additional point, Your Honour, is of course that the witness in answering not the question that Mr. Margetts had asked was in fact reading from his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So I put a marker here in relation to 89(F) and how careful we need to be with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 144, Mr. Margetts just read to you a part of your statement concerning a meeting you had and asked then whether there were any further contacts. You answered that question but then returned to the meeting and described it again, and it was already read out to you. We are under some time constraints. May I instruct you, first of all, to carefully listen to what exactly Mr. Margetts' question is and then to answer that question, because of course we have your statement. And second, not to -- when you answer a question, not to further read from your statement, but tell us what you know. Yes? Please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Witness, when you were detained, was Mr. Komljenovic mentioned to you by anyone whom you were detained with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: What was said to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: In relation to Komljenovic, I know that together with me in prison there were two of his brothers-in-law. One of them was called Anto and the other, Ilija Zeba. Komljenovic's wife, who was a Croat, came to the prison to visit the husbands of her sisters, and she told him that Komljenovic had said that they could not be released and go back to Kotor Varos. The only thing that could be done was to take them to Travnik, in a convoy. That was what I heard from Ilija Zeba, who is Komljenovic's brother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Following your receipt of that information, did the brothers-in-law remain detained or were they released?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: They were taken in a convoy to Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with that exhibit of 27 March.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: If the witness, Your Honour, could be provided with the next exhibit, which is dated 7 April 1992, and if that exhibit could be provided under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit number P332, under seal. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Witness, in your statement you refer at paragraphs 97, 98, and 99, to your membership at the National Defence Council. I'm not asking you to refer to that now, but just reminding you that that is in the statement. I refer to this excerpt from the minutes of the National Defence Council of Kotor Varos of 7 April 1992. Can you look at item 2, the entry for item 2, and tell me whether you were present at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Can I refer you again to item 2, where it says that there was a reference to a problem of unfair treatment of Muslim and Croatian staff. Could you explain to the Court what that problem of unfair treatment was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: I held a post as one of the leaders in that company. In that period of time, the managing director came to see me and told me that I would no longer stay in my position as manager, but he said, "You would not be out of a job. You will stay on as an advisor." Those sub-managers who were subordinate to me would take over what I used to do, he said. I asked to have a decision in writing, because a thing like this could only be decided by an official body within the company. Needless to say, I never received any decision in writing. A similar situation arose also in relation to one of the foremen at Brigadirnica [phoen], who was a Croat by ethnicity. His name was Nedeljko Brgic [phoen]. I asked my manager whether he had received any orders from anyone to dismiss Croats and Muslims from leading positions. The situation was similar in other companies too at the time. He avoided answering me in relation to my question, who the orders had come from. But all of us who had been dismissed knew what the real truth behind that was, that Croats and Muslims could not hold managerial posts in the company.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you refer to the paragraph that lies above the heading item 2 and commences after remarks by Savo Tepic. This paragraph continues and states that: "After the remarks by Savo Tepic, chief of the SJB in Kotor Varos on the conclusions of the meeting held on 6 April 1992 at the security services centre in Banja Luka, others also took part in a discussion on the transformation in the Kotor Varos SJB, and it was agreed that a meeting would take place with Stojan Zupljanin." Can you describe for the Court what you observed in terms of the transformation in the Kotor Varos SJB.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Already by that date, the public security service of the Banja Luka region was cut off from Sarajevo in terms of communication lines. The surrounding municipalities that were within the Serbian autonomous district, that is, within the Serbian Republic, received their commands from Banja Luka and they started wearing their insignia. The public security service in Kotor Varos did not agree with the idea of joining the security services centre in Banja Luka, although it continued communicating with the services there because it had no choice. And the public security service in Kotor Varos bore the insignia of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Did that change at any time; that is, did the Kotor Varos SJB continue to bear the insignia of Bosnia and Herzegovina or did it at some time change its insignia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: No. It kept the insignia that it had from before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The takeover of Kotor Varos took place on the 11th of June, 1992. After this date, what insignia did the police in Kotor Varos wear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Following the 11th of July 1992, the police in Kotor Varos started wearing the insignia of the Serbian Republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Witness, could you again tell the Court -- or could you please tell the Court what date Kotor Varos was taken over.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: The takeover took place on the 11th of June in 1992. Yes, exactly. 11th of June, 1992. It was my mistake before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Just for clarity then: Is it your answer that after the 11th of June, 1992, the police in Kotor Varos started wearing the insignia of the Serbian Republic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Just a marker again, Your Honour. It really is an inappropriate way of asking a question to include in it the assertion in that leading format the takeover of Kotor Varos took place on the 11th of June. Interestingly enough, Mr. Margetts didn't get the response he wanted. He got the 11th of July and is still trying to sort of clarify that. But it really is better letting the witness giving the answer than telling them in the question when the takeover took place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, objection is about leading too much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the reason for the clarification is that the witness statement contains references to the date of the takeover, and that will be admitted into evidence. Accordingly, non-leading questions were asked to clarify the matter, which the witness did eminently by himself. And finally, a leading question was asked merely to repeat what the witness clearly intended by his prior answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll just have a look. Yes. I do understand why you did it. In general terms, I would say that using a witness statement when we examine a witness viva voce we should refrain to just ask him to repeat what is in his statement but this is not exactly what happened here. So therefore, if you would please keep in mind the objection and what I just said and then you may now proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: If I could refer you, Witness, to the first paragraph in the minutes dated 7 April 1992, there is a reference there to a Lieutenant Colonel Peulic. Do you know this person, and if so, could you describe who he is to the Court.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes, I do know the person. He was commander of the Yugoslav People's Army for the area of Skender Vakuf, Kotor Varos, and Celinac. He attended twice the meetings of the -- of national defence, where I was present as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Witness, if I could refer you to the next paragraph, and there is a reference to Slobodan Zupljanin. Could you please describe to the Court when you first met Slobodan Zupljanin and who he is. And could we go into private session for the answer to this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, could the witness be shown the next two exhibits, that is, an exhibit dated 24 May 1992 and an exhibit dated 1st June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: In regard to the exhibit dated 1st June 1992, I note that that already has a Prosecution exhibit number, and that is P188.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There's no [Realtime transcript read in error "I'll"] need to assign another number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps I expressed myself poorly when I said I'll need to assign. I said no need to assign another number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Witness, do you have before you a document headed "meeting of the Garici branch office," which is in handwriting? Witness, could you look at the first -- or the second paragraph on that document, which is marked with the number 1, and states: "The commander of the Maslovare military unit, Slobodan Zupljanin, informed the citizens." Is that accurate? Was Slobodan Zupljanin the commander of the Maslovare unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Could I refer you further down in the minutes of this meeting to comments made by one Ibrahim Nusinovic wherein he asked what the role of the military unit stationed at Maslovare would be if Kotor Varos were united with the Krajina and if the party leaderships did not reach an agreement. Witness, what was the situation in the Krajina and what was the organisation of this unit at that time, and did you see any role for that unit at that time?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it might be better if that question is broken up one at a time rather than giving the witness a compound question of that nature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, would you follow that suggestion, or would you think the question should be put in the way that you did?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was content with the question. I think the witness could understand it and provide a reasonable answer, but I'm happy also to abide by my learned friend's suggestions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Witness, what -- as at 24 May 1992, what role did you think the Maslovare unit could play?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: This unit was mobilised mostly from the ranks of ethnic Serbs. There were only few Muslims and Croats there who mostly came from mixed marriages. The role of this unit was to ensure peace and security in the area of Kotor Varos municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: In light of the situation in the Krajina, if agreement was not reached between the parties, what role may have this unit composed chiefly of Serbs played?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object on the basis of -- it's speculative and it's also -- has the danger of being rather a tendentious question in the sense of looking back as opposed to the view at the time. The witness has given his view at the time, but I would object, both on the basis of the speculative nature of the question and the inherent danger of forming conclusions based on subsequent events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 144, you've seen and it has been read to you what Mr. Ibrahim Nusinovic asked at that time about the role of the military units stationed in Maslovare. Did you at that time have an answer to the question that was put by Mr. Nusinovic? Would you know an answer to that question? If so, please give it to us. If not, please tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this period of time, in the surrounding municipalities that had not joined the Serbian Republic, we heard some information over Radio Zagreb that there were clashes between the army and the Muslim and Croat populations. And this citizens [as interpreted] put this question quite rightly, because he was concerned that the same role would be assumed by this particular army unit that was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: What specific role was he concerned that this army unit would perform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: This unit could have been used for the purposes of the Serbian army and not as a Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Was this unit later used for the purposes of the Serbian army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to refer the witness to the next exhibit that he has before him, which is Exhibit 188.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Witness, I'd like you to look at the last page of the document, and moving backwards, refer to the fourth paragraph from the bottom of the document. This paragraph reads as follows. It refers to the positions of the 122nd Light Brigade and states: "Some of the forces from this unit sealed off Kotor Varos where division had occurred within the SDA ranks. Some of the armed extremists want armed operations, while some of the decent Muslims are in favour of peaceful coexistence with the Serbs." As at 1 June 1992, was there division within the SDA ranks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: As at 1st June 1992, did some members of the SDA want armed operations or did they not?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, perhaps, Your Honour, we also require there "to your knowledge."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, if you ask a question to a witness, if it's not about himself, it's always to the witness's knowledge. So I think that that goes without saying. If not really needed, I would rather you to let Mr. Margetts put the questions he wants. And if there's really some technical issue that of course you can object, but this was one which was not really necessary. Please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I don't mind losing the occasional one, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Witness, I'll restate the question. As at 1st June 1992, were there members at the SDA in Kotor Varos who wanted armed operations to begin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: No, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Why was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: The Muslims wanted to have peace in Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: As at 1st June 1992, what was the situation for the Muslims in Kotor Varos in terms of their association with neighbouring municipalities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: You mean the relations among the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: No, not the relations among the Muslims, but in terms of the preceding question relating to the desire of the Muslims to avoid armed operations, what did the Muslims anticipate if armed operations occurred in the area of Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: The Muslims in Kotor Varos were afraid of possible armed conflicts around Kotor Varos. That's why we suggested that the municipality of Kotor Varos remain neutral until such time as the final solution is found in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Because we're a small municipality that doesn't mean anything to anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next exhibit is a video exhibit, and there are various are excerpts that I'd like to play from the video. We may be able to play one of those excerpts prior to the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you think you could do that in the next five minutes, we'll start then with the first excerpt.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Let's proceed, then, if we can, with the next video extract, which is the next exhibit listed.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit number P334.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would that be for the whole of the video or just for the first excerpt?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I understand, currently we have five excerpts, so if they could be numbered .1 through to .5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So this one then would be -- the whole of it would be P334 and the first part to be played would be P334.1

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm just corrected on that. There are in fact six excerpts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. 1 to 6 then. Well, during the break I take it that some solution will be found by Madam Registrar, your case manager. We'll play the first video part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have to ask to stop this playing of the video. We need the translation to be read as well, because it will be then translated into French. But if it's just on our screen, we'll only have the B/C/S, no English appears in the transcript. So could we restart that. And did you provide the interpreters with the text of the -- otherwise they can read it on the bottom of the -- of course, they can listen and read it at the bottom of the video, although it's always to be preferred if they have a hard copy in front of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. They have been provided with a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps you should have interrupted me immediately and said yes, they have been provided with that. So the explanation why it's important was not needed, therefore, any more. Could we restart, and could I ask the interpreters to read aloud for the transcript the English text.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is taking a little bit longer than I had anticipated. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's finish this first one then and have a break.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] The mopping up operations in the area around Kotor Varos continued today. In a lightning operation, members of a special detachment of the Banja Luka security services centre and the army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina took Bilice, one of the best fortified strongholds of the Croat extremists. The specials and the army had only one person injured in this operation whereas the enemy had some 50 fatalities and a large number of wounded. The mopping up continues, and there are only three entrenched strongholds of the Croat Muslim outlaws left. In the town itself the situation is gradually returning to normal. Although movement is still allowed only from 9 to 11.00, life is slowly returning to the streets of Kotor Varos. Yesterday Muslim and Croat forces allegedly wanted to negotiate with the Serb side about the cessation of war and establishing peace in these parts. The army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the police accepted the invitation and set off for the meeting, believing that an understanding was possible. Only a few kilometres from Kotor Varos, our concealed hosts, Muslim extremists, waited hidden in ambushes and treacherously and perfidiously opened fire on the army and police troops. In this perfidious attack one person was killed and a number of specials and soldiers wounded. Today Captain Slobodan Zupljanin is also in the Banja Luka hospital. We first went to visit Captain Zupljanin, who is currently ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Witness, you've seen that segment. Were you aware of any armed combat operations that were taking place between Muslim and Serb forces in Kotor Varos in 1992, and if so, how did you become aware?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes. From the area in which I lived, I saw the village of Bilice being attacked, which was referred to in this excerpt that we have just seen. Likewise, you could see clashes, or rather, the shelling of villages along the slopes of the mountains surrounding Kotor Varos itself. Those were Muslim villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I have no further questions on that matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll have a break until a quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was informed that as far as the exhibit number concerns, that the video, in contradiction to what I said before the break, will have one number, and the transcript will have that same number, and the letter "A" added. Madam Registrar, that would then be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit number P334 for the CD and P334.A for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I also do understand that the transcript has been provided to us now in a different form and that we'll get the B/C/S version in a similar form. But only by today. Although the text as such is already available now to Mr. Krajisnik. Yes, please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's the English translation that is in the appropriate form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And it is the B/C/S transcript that is -- will be replaced tomorrow in the appropriate form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I'd like to play the second part of the video, if I could.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] To be quite frank, I supposed that it could happen and we could be waylaid, but we never expected it at that place because the place we were supposed to go to, we were to meet at, is much better for an ambush. So that it came as a surprise. I am aware, though, after all the situations in the West Slavonian theatre of war from which I had come that the enemy will resort to any method, any means, any way to destroy and liquidate us systematically, step by step."

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the man depicted on that segment of the video?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes, I do. That is Slobodan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: You've previously described to the Court who Slobodan Zupljanin is. After June 1992, and before December 1992, did you at any time meet with Slobodan Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Where were you at the time, and could you describe to the Court the meeting.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: At that time, I was detained in the municipal prison behind the court building in Kotor Varos. Ahmed Cirkic and myself were placed in front of the bars in the prison itself, and on the other side of the bars there was Slobodan Zupljanin and Muhamed Sadikovic. It was then that I found out that Muhamed Sadikovic and those who opposed the Serb army had handed over their weapons, that they would be taken to Travnik. Zupljanin brought Sadikovic there for him to see that both myself and Ahmed Cirkic were still alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: At approximately what date did that meeting occur?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: It may have been in late November. I can't remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Whilst you were detained from July 1992 through to December 1992, did any of the guards mention to you Slobodan Zupljanin, and if so, in what context?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes, there was a reference to him. In the elementary school building, where I was first detained, on several occasions, groups of Muslims were brought in from the Vrbanjci area, more specifically, Hanifici and Dabovci. Guards would enter the hall. It was a gym. And whatever they were told, the rest of us could hear too. The guards told the people assembled there that their release or their transport by convoys would be decided by Slobodan Zupljanin and that it hinged upon his decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'd like to play the third part of the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so, with the assistance of the technicians.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] On this occasion, I want to point out that we have met with outstanding cooperation even among those people, but unfortunately, our experience in two villages where we managed to reach an understanding was that units of the interior ministry of the Serb Republic of Krajina and members of my unit were fired on from these villages so that we had to respond appropriately.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the person depicted in that segment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is Lieutenant Colonel Peulic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: You've previously described to the Court who Lieutenant Colonel Bosko Peulic was. Was any reference made to him by anyone during the course of your detention in Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes. The detainees who were being brought in from the Vrbanjci area said that this Serb unit in the Kotor Varos area was commanded by Peulic, that he was the main commander of that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I'd like to play the next part of the video.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] Mr. Brdjanin, tell us: Why did you come and how do you see the latest developments in the Kotor Varos municipality? Mr. Brdjanin: Let me tell you, my duty as the president of the Crisis Staff of the autonomous region is to visit all the fronts. I must admit that most of the time I was in the corridor leading to Serbia, but simply, my visit, the reason for my coming here is that every Monday I must inform the presidents of all the crisis staffs about the political situation in this area. We must clean up our area, which unquestionably includes Kotor Varos and Jajce. And the most important battle which is under way and which I attended yesterday is the breakthrough to Serbia. Simply, we can see for ourselves that there can be no more negotiations with those waging war against us. Those who took up arms must be defeated, hand themselves over, and total Serb authority must rule here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Do you recognise the person depicted in that segment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes. That is Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Did you ever meet with Radoslav Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: No. I know him from the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: At the conclusion of his comments, he said that "total Serb authority must rule here," referring to the area of Kotor Varos. As at July 1992, was that the situation in Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I'd like to play the next segment of the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] We requested the political structures to do whatever is necessary to avoid possible conflicts when facilities could be destroyed, where people could get killed and so on. However, I must say that the other side has accepted this activity of ours, at least in part. A number of extremists, however, have taken to the woods and refuse to place themselves under control or to return weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the speaker in that segment, and if so, can you describe who he is and what he is role was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise the speaker. The speaker is Stojan Zupljanin. Up to the conflict, he used to be the chief of the security services centre in Banja Luka. He hails from Maslovare local commune, Kotor Varos municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: After the conflict began, what was his role?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: I believe he retained his previous position, the one that he had held up to the beginning of conflict, as chief of the security services centre in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to play the final segment of the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] This surprise visit by the Krajina leadership to the Serbian soldiers testifies to a synchronised cooperation. The officers and men of the Serbian armed formations, in addition to activities for the liberation of the Serb territories, are also directly involved in the establishment of a corridor to Serbia as one of the greatest operations in the history of the Serb people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Witness 144, the camera in that segment panned from right to left, and there were a number of people sitting at the table. Did you recognise any of those people, and if so, who did you recognise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes. First of all, I recognised Radoslav Brdjanin. Next to him, there was a person seated that looked to me like Radovan Karadzic. Further, there was a person called Savo Tepic, and next to him, Mane Tepic, his brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Who was Savo Tepic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Before the beginning of the clashes in Kotor Varos, Savo Tepic was chief of the public security service in Kotor Varos, a position in which he remained following the outbreak of clashes. But by then, it was a Serb police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Who was Mane Tepic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Before the outbreak of clashes in Kotor Varos, Mane Tepic was the chief of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: After the outbreak of clashes, do you know what role Mane Tepic occupied?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Before we leave the video, I would just like to refer you to the concluding remarks in the segment that depicted Captain Slobodan Zupljanin and ask for your comment in respect of those remarks. Zupljanin stated that: "The enemy would resort to any method, any means, any way to destroy and liquidate us systematically, step by step." As at July 1992, were you aware of any systematic plan to eliminate the Serbs in Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, could you replay the last excerpt from the video?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] This surprise visit by the Krajina leadership to the Serbian soldiers testifies to a synchronised cooperation. The officers and men of the Serbian armed formations, in addition to activities for the liberation of the Serb territories, are also directly involved in the establishment of a corridor to Serbia as one of the greatest operations in the history of the Serb people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber asked for it, Mr. Margetts, because the Chamber wanted to understand the testimony, especially in respect of recognition of Mr. Karadzic. Could you perhaps have that replayed and perhaps stop it at the place where the witness thinks he recognises Mr. Karadzic, so that we can at least follow his testimony in more detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We will attempt to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I know that it's sometimes difficult, but ... Witness, could I ask you: Whenever the point comes that you see the person you said you thought you recognised as Mr. Karadzic, would you then please say "stop" so that we can try to stop the video picture so that you can explain which person you thought you recognised as Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand that your testimony is that the person we just saw in the middle of the video picture where it stopped, that, in your opinion, you recognised Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I said it appeared to me that this might be Karadzic, which means I'm not 100 per cent certain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I understood that, that you were not certain, but you thought it was him. Thank you very much. Please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I'd like to present to the witness the next exhibit, which is the exhibit dated 15 August.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit number P335.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I just ask the registrar to check that exhibit and see that it is the 54th session of the War Presidency dated 15 August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We received, and I see Madam Registrar has the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, I noticed that in many, many translations, names are in capitals, where they do not appear in the original as capitals. I'm not asking you to change all that, but even in one of the documents we see that -- and I'm referring to P332, under item 2, that even what seems to be the family name is not in capitals, but the first name. So even mistakes are made in making the family names in capitals. It's not a major issue, but we don't need any changes in the translation, especially because you do not recognise any more where in the original capitals are used.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. We will take note of those comments and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not to change everything, but it doesn't add anything. It confuses only.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Witness 144, this document that is before you is the extract from the minutes of the 54th session of the War Presidency, held on 15 August 1992, and it's signed by Nedjeljko Djekanovic. Could you describe for me who Nedjeljko Djekanovic is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: I met Nedjeljko Djekanovic (redacted) (redacted). He became president of the SDS. Nedjeljko Djekanovic was a Kotor Varos deputy to the Republican Assembly. Nedjeljko Djekanovic also became president of the Crisis Staff following the outbreak of clashes in Kotor Varos. Up to the outbreak, he had been a delegate in the Municipal Assembly of Kotor Varos also.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: After the elections in late 1990, who was elected to be the deputy in the republican assembly from Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Nedjeljko Djekanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: After the assembly of the Serbian people was formed at the republican level, did Nedjeljko Djekanovic join that assembly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I'd like to refer you to item 2 in this document that is before you, and you will see the last two paragraphs of this document refer to a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. report from battalion commander Zupljanin. He refers to an attack by extremists. In the final paragraph it reads as follows: "As regards the group of civilians taken out of the Vrbanjci area, instructions were given that they be transported to Vlasic in the course of the day and sent towards Travnik." Is that consistent with anything you heard during 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I'd also like to refer you to the first paragraph of item 2, where it refers to Savo Tepic and the fact that he spoke of the situation in the SJB, public security station, or, more precisely, about the security situation, as at August 1992. You've previously described to the Court who Savo Tepic was. Between July and August 1992, did you see Savo Tepic, and if so, where did you see him and what was he doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes, I did see him. I saw him the next day after my arrest, at the Kotor Varos public security station. I saw him, and he came to our place of detention in the school building. They would take us from the school building to clean the toilets at the public security station. So while I was doing that, I saw Savo. He was going about his duties as chief of the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: During the course of your detention at the school, did you see him present in the school building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes. On one occasion, he came to visit the guards as we were cleaning the guards' room. They would take us out to clean their room.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: What was the nature of the relationship between Savo Tepic and the guards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: I assume that he gave them orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I'd just like to refer you back to the final paragraph of item 2, wherein it commences: "As regards the group of civilians taken out of the Vrbanjci area." You stated that you heard about this matter. Can you describe the group of civilians and what nationality they were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: There was a group of civilians that was brought to the elementary school in Kotor Varos from the Hanifici area. This group stayed with us for several days. They told us that their wives and children had been arrested separately and taken to a different place, after which they had been deported to Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: What nationality was this group of civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: They were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to present the next exhibit to this witness. It's the document dated 8 August 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit number P336.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Witness, this is a precis of the minutes of the 51st meeting of the War Presidency, held on 8 August 1992 in Kotor Varos. At item 4, the second matter reads as follows. It states: "Savo reported on the unsanitary conditions in the prison." Can you tell the Court who you think Savo would be.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: I assume this must be Savo Tepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The reference refers to unsanitary conditions in the prison. Whilst you were detained in the prison, were the conditions unsanitary, and if so, could you describe them to the Court.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: Yes. The conditions were unsanitary. We were put up in the elementary school building. There were over a hundred detainees there. There was no running water. It wasn't possible for us to wash ourselves. We were taken to the toilet by the guards, and the pipes didn't work properly. We were given drinking water every second day. We would share among ourselves whatever we were given. We were given a crate of fruit juice which amounted to about two decilitres per day per prisoners. We slept rough on the floor. I had traces of blood on my body, because I had been beaten and tortured. I was unable to wash these off for more than two months, simply because there was no water. This would be a thumbnail sketch of the unsanitary conditions in the prison. Once in this prison in the elementary school building, there was a man who came and walked into the hall in which we were detained. He told us that he was stationed with his unit at the medical centre, a building which was just behind the school building. He did not beat us, but he realised what our situation was, and he had a word with the guards, telling the guards to allow us to at least wash ourselves, because there was a danger. He told them that we could infect them too. He stated his name. I did not remember his name, but I remember precisely that he said he was from Krusevac, which is a town in Serbia. He said, "I can hardly wait to leave this place and go back to my wife and children, and I wish you could do the same as soon as possible too."

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your answer describes the conditions in the elementary school building. What were the conditions like in the prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: After I had spent two months at the school, we were transferred to the building of the municipal prison there, situated behind the building of the court. Upon our arrival there, I was put up into room number 1, where there was some 50 detainees. The area of the room was some 4.5 by 6.5 metres. There was no room for us to lie down. The doors were locked. We were taken to the toilets by the guards when they thought or saw it fitting. There was no water at all in the prison, and the water was supplied to us in the same way as in the school when we were detained there. There were many detainees in the prison, a great many of them. Those who were in room number 1 before I had arrived there told me that there was some 80 of them. We slept on the floor. We used the little space that we had. We were crowded like sardines. Preferably someone had to stand up in order for the others to lie down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to present to the witness the next two exhibits, the first exhibit being the document dated 15 June 1992, and the second dated 20 June 1992. And if the second document could be provided under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The first document will be P337, and the second document, P338, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Witness 144, could I refer you to the first document with the cover page stating "decision permitting citizens freedom of movement in the town from 9.00 a.m. to 11.00 a.m." And I note that this is a decision of the Crisis Staff of Kotor Varos dated 15 June 1992. I'd like to refer you to the first paragraph, and it states that: "Citizens are hereby permitted freedom of movement in the town from 9.00 a.m. to 11.00 a.m." Were you informed of this decision?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
utterances.text: With the establishment of the Crisis Staff and after the takeover of Kotor Varos by the Serbs, a fire engine passed through the town that had a megaphone placed on it, and there they informed the citizens of the establishment of the Crisis Staff and of the rules regulating their freedom of movement. And with the emphasis on the freedom of movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Was the information provided consistent with this decision of 15 June 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ 144
